notes: Surfnerd overview: Pipeline & Backdoor is the most famous wave on the planet, a heaving barrel that detonates over an uneven lava-slab reef only about 80 metres off Ehukai Beach Park on Oahu's North Shore. It's really two waves sharing one peak: Pipeline, the legendary left, and Backdoor, the super-hollow right that funnels across the shallow reef toward Off-The-Wall. Outer reefs refract and focus arriving swell onto the inside reef, so a wave that looks absent on a flat day can come roaring back to life when the right swell shows up. It's rated among the best waves in the world. Skill (surfnerd): Expert. Surf-forecast Pipeline_1: "Pipeline in Oahu is an exposed reef break that has fairly consistent surf, although summer tends to be mostly flat. The best wind direction is from the southeast. Most of the surf here comes from groundswells and the best swell direction is from the west northwest. Often Crowded. Watch out for rocks and locals." Surf-forecast Backdoor-5: "Backdoor in Oahu is an exposed reef break that has quite reliable surf, although summer tends to be mostly flat. Works best in offshore winds from the southeast. Clean groundswells prevail and the ideal swell angle is from the northwest. A popular wave that can get growded. Watch out for - Rocks." Surf-forecast Banzai-Pipelines-and-Backdoor: "Banzai Pipelines and Backdoor in Oahu is an exposed reef break that has quite reliable surf, although summer tends to be mostly flat. Offshore winds are from the east southeast. Groundswells more frequent than windswells and the best swell direction is from the northwest. Reef breaks provide lefts and rights. Good surf at all stages of the tide. Often Crowded. Beware of rips and rocks." Wannasurf pipeline: quality Totally Epic; experience Pros or kamikaze only...; wave Reef-coral, Left; swell size Starts working at 1.0m-1.5m / 3ft-5ft and holds up to 4m+ / 12ft; crowd weekday Crowded, weekend Ultra crowded. Wannasurf backdoor: quality Totally Epic; experience Experienced surfers; wave Reef-coral, Right; swell size Starts working at 1.5m-2m /5ft-6ft and holds up to 5m / 16 ft and over; crowd weekday Crowded, weekend Ultra crowded. Access (surfnerd): Ehukai Beach Park sits right in front of the break, with a car park offering free parking plus roadside parking, though spaces fill fast when the surf is good. Facilities include restrooms, showers, and lifeguards on the beach. notes: Surfnerd overview: Sunset isn't one wave but a whole arena of sections spread across a huge playing field of uneven reef. It's a waterman's wave, where open-ocean power unloads and surfers swap equipment and adjust their approach to suit the reef's wide variability and moody nature. The zone runs from Val's Reef and the Inside Bowl to the West Peak, The Point, and Backyards, each section breaking differently depending on the day. Both lefts and rights show up, and the water is clean, clear, and blue. Skill (surfnerd): Expert. When it's working here, it can get crowded. Beware of rocks and locals."
